ety.text: Originally a variant spelling of Russian айда (ajda), also compare Ukrainian гайда (hajda). Originally the word was supposed to have stress on the second syllable, but was later reanalyzed as having stress on the initial syllable. Ultimately from a Turkic language; compare Ottoman Turkish هایده (hayde). The word is attested in foreign sources since the XVI century. First appears in Russian literature around 19th century, possibly a learned borrowing from the term in the foreign source.
